previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis and sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted for recurrent epigastric abdominal pain and nausea. She presented with poor oral intake and was managed with IV fluids, bowel rest, and continuation of her home pain and anxiety medications. Her lipase was mildly elevated at 103, consistent with mild acute pancreatitis, but she improved quickly without need for ERCP. She tolerated a regular diet, remained hemodynamically stable, and had no complications. Constipation was anticipated and managed with her usual bowel regimen. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her GI and primary care providers and to monitor for worsening symptoms.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year-old woman with a history of recurrent 
pancreatitis thought to be due to Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, 
appendectomy, and hearing impairment, who presented with 
abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea. She had a lipase of 86 and 
normal LFTs. She was managed conservatively for possible 
pancreatitis with IV fluids, bowel rest, pain and nausea control 
with symptomatic improvement. She tolerated a soft diet and was 
discharged home.

# Abdominal Pain: Pt with chronic pancreatitis, likely secondary 
to sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, who presented with acute 
epigastric pain, nausea, and diarrhea. This was very typical of 
her prior bouts of pancreatitis, with a lipase of 86, on the 
lower end of previous measurements of her lipase. She did not 
meet SIRs criteria or have any evidence of organ failure. LFTS 
WNL and bili WNL. Physical exam benign. She was managed 
conservatively for possible pancreatitis with IV fluids, bowel 
rest, pain and nausea control with symptomatic improvement. She 
tolerated a soft diet and was discharged home.

# Anxiety, depression, PTSD: Continued home venlafaxine, 
imipramine, trazodone, prazosin, and clonazepam.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___, 

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your hospital stay 
at ___.

You came to the hospital with abdominal pain, nausea, and 
diarrhea, which you felt were similar to past episodes of yours 
of pancreatitis.   Given your symptoms and the fact that you had 
a mildly elevated lipase level, we treated you for a possible 
episode of pancreatitis.  We gave you IV fluids, nutrition as 
you were able to tolerate, pain medications, and nausea 
medications. Your symptoms have improved and you were able to 
tolerate food.

Please keep any outpatient follow-up appointments for which you 
are scheduled, and take all of your medications as prescribed. 
Please seek medical attention if you develop fevers, chills, 
worsening abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, blood in 
your stool, black stool, dehydration, inability to eat, or any 
other symptoms that concern you.
